name: WPMozo Wishlist – WooCommerce Wishlist & Save for Later
author: Elicus

sections.description:
WPMozo Wishlist Lite is a free WooCommerce wishlist plugin that lets shoppers save a product while browsing or move an item out of their cart to buy later. Enable guest wishlists so visitors can start saving before they create an account. When they sign in, they can link those products to their account.

Give shoppers a wishlist page where they can revisit saved items, see which ones have dropped in price, and add a product to their cart. As a store owner, you can also see which products appear on the most wishlists.

Try the wishlist demo | Read the setup guide

Add wishlist buttons to your store

  • Place an Add to Wishlist button on product, shop, and category pages. Show it on the product image or before or after Add to Cart.
  • Choose text, an icon, or both. Adjust colors, labels, and notifications in WooCommerce settings.
  • Add a button to a custom product loop with [wpmozo_add_to_wishlist_button]. To show a button for a specific product, pass its ID, for example [wpmozo_add_to_wishlist_button product_id="123"].

Let shoppers save cart items for later

Move to Wishlist works with the WooCommerce Cart block and the classic cart. Place the action beside the remove icon or under the product name. If you want shoppers to see the words “Save for later,” choose the text or text-and-icon style and edit the label.

Build a wishlist page

  • Add the Wishlists block to a page and use its grid controls to set the columns and spacing. You can also display saved products with the [wpmozo_wishlists] shortcode.
  • Show a price-drop badge when an item costs less than it did when the shopper saved it. Customize the badge text, size, and color.
  • Shoppers can add or remove favorites without reloading the page and undo a removal on the wishlist page. When the list is empty, send them back to your shop, a selected page, or a custom URL.

Find your most wishlisted products

Open WooCommerce > Wishlist Insights > Popular Products to see how many wishlists include each product. Search for a product or sort the report by wishlist count. This report is included in Lite.

What does Pro add?

WPMozo Wishlist for WooCommerce Pro includes the following features.

  • Multiple named wishlists per customer, with private lists and public lists shoppers can share by link, email, WhatsApp, Facebook, or X.
  • The ability to save a specific variation, including its selected size or color, image, price, and stock status.
  • Item quantities, bulk actions, extra wishlist icons, and button tooltips.
  • Tools to see who saved a product and to open, search, and manage individual customers’ wishlists.

Support and feedback

Ask a question or suggest a feature in the support forum. If you have used the plugin on your store, you can leave a review.

Follow WPMozo on Facebook and YouTube, or Elicus on X.

Related Plugins

For WooCommerce product layouts, see WPMozo Product Carousel and WPMozo Product Grid. For the page editor, see WPMozo Addons Lite for Elementor and WPMozo Blocks and Addons.

sections.installation:
Minimum requirements

  • WordPress 6.4 or higher
  • WooCommerce 7.7.0 or higher
  • PHP 7.0 or higher
  • MySQL 5.6 or higher, or MariaDB 10.1 or higher

Install and set up

  1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. In Plugins > Add New, search for WPMozo Wishlist Lite for WooCommerce. Select Install Now, then Activate. If you already have the plugin ZIP, use Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin to install it.
  3. Open WooCommerce > Settings > Wishlist. In General, choose who can use wishlists. In Buttons, choose where the buttons appear. Select Save changes after editing a tab.
  4. Create a wishlist page with the Wishlists block or [wpmozo_wishlists], publish it, and link to it from your store menu.
  5. Visit a product, save it, and open the wishlist page to check the result. To check guest access, use a signed-out browser window.

Updating

Back up your site before updating.
sections.faq:
Can guests save products without logging in?

Yes. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Wishlist > General, uncheck Enable Wishlist for logged in users only, and save your changes. This setting is checked on a fresh Lite installation. With guest wishlists enabled, a browser cookie identifies the guest’s wishlist. When the shopper logs in, they can choose to link their saved products to their account.

Can shoppers save items for later from the WooCommerce Cart block?

Yes. The Cart block and the classic cart both support Move to Wishlist. In WooCommerce > Settings > Wishlist > Buttons, find Move to Wishlist Cart to choose its position and style. To change the wording to “Save for later,” edit Move to Wishlist text under Texts.

How do I create a WooCommerce wishlist page?

Create a page named Wishlist and insert the Wishlists block. If you use a shortcode, paste [wpmozo_wishlists] into a Shortcode block instead. Publish the page and add it to your store navigation so shoppers can find their saved products.

Can I see which products shoppers save most often?

Yes. The Popular Products report under WooCommerce > Wishlist Insights is included in Lite. Sort by Wishlists to compare products. Pro also lets you see which customers saved a product and manage their individual wishlists.

How does the price-drop badge work?

For a simple product, the badge shows how much its price has dropped since the shopper saved it. Turn it on or off under WooCommerce > Settings > Wishlist > General. In WooCommerce > Settings > Wishlist, open Texts to change the wording or Styles to change the font size and color.

What can I customize, and which themes does the plugin support?

You can change button placement, labels, colors, and whether the button shows text, an icon, or both under WooCommerce > Settings > Wishlist. Lite includes integrations for Astra, Blocksy, Kadence, Hestia, OceanWP, and Woostify. For a custom product layout, the button shortcode lets you choose where the button appears.

Can a customer’s wishlist data be exported or erased?

Yes. For registered customers, use Tools > Export Personal Data or Tools > Erase Personal Data. The Delete Wishlists when a user is deleted option also removes lists when you delete the account. It is enabled by default. Suggested privacy policy text is available under Settings > Privacy > Policy Guide.

Guest wishlists are identified by browser cookies. The email-based export and erasure tools cover registered customers. Expired guest wishlists are removed during scheduled cleanup.

Where can I get help or report a security issue?

For setup questions and feature requests, use the WordPress.org support forum. Report security vulnerabilities privately through the Patchstack Vulnerability Disclosure Program.
sections.changelog:
2026-11-20 – Version 2.1.0
* ADDED: Move to Wishlist button on the Cart block, beside the remove icon or under the product name, following the same position and type settings as the classic cart.
* ADDED: Wishlists in WordPress’s personal data tools: Tools > Export Personal Data includes a user’s wishlists and saved products, and Tools > Erase Personal Data deletes them and reports how many it deleted.
* ADDED: Suggested privacy policy text under Settings > Privacy > Policy Guide, describing what the wishlist stores, who can see it and how long it is kept, following the plugin’s settings.
* ADDED: “Delete Wishlists when a user is deleted” setting, on by default, to delete a user’s wishlists along with their account.
* ADDED: Undo Notice settings under WooCommerce > Settings > Wishlist > Styles, for the background, text and delete icon colors, the text size, and the Undo button’s background color, text color and text size.
* ADDED: On Product Image, a new position for the product page’s wishlist button, in the top left or top right corner of the main image and below the theme’s zoom icon or sale badge when one is in that corner.
* IMPROVEMENT: Declared compatibility with the WooCommerce Cart and Checkout blocks.
* IMPROVEMENT: The wishlist stylesheet and script, and the CSS from the Styles settings, load only on pages that can show a wishlist button or wishlist, and the script is deferred to the footer instead of blocking the page from rendering.
* IMPROVEMENT: Redesigned the notice shown after removing a product from the wishlist, with a frosted glass look, a clearer Undo button and a countdown to when the removal becomes final.
* FIXED: Resolved an issue where moving a product variation from the classic cart to the wishlist left it in the cart.
* FIXED: Resolved an issue where deleting a site on a multisite network left its wishlist tables in the database.
* FIXED: Resolved an issue where, on Twenty Twenty-One, the On Product Image wishlist button at its default Top Right position appeared just left of each product in product grids, rather than on its image.
* FIXED: Resolved an issue where product loops on block themes outside the shop and category templates, such as a [products] shortcode or a page builder’s products widget, didn’t show the wishlist button.
* FIXED: Resolved an issue where, on a block theme whose shop or product templates use WooCommerce’s Classic Template block, the shop and category pages showed no wishlist buttons, and nor did out-of-stock product pages.
* FIXED: Resolved an issue where Product Collection and Products blocks placed on a page didn’t show the wishlist button on classic themes, or on block themes whose shop uses WooCommerce’s Classic Template block.
* FIXED: Resolved an issue where text settings saved in version 2.0.0 with an apostrophe or quote kept a backslash in front of it after updating, showing Don\’t for Don’t until the text was retyped. Those settings are cleaned up once on update.
* FIXED: Resolved an issue where, on a translated site, saving the settings stored any default text whose translation contains an apostrophe or ampersand, so later translation updates didn’t reach it.
* FIXED: Resolved an issue where products deleted from the store were still counted in a wishlist’s pages and in Wishlist Insights, though the wishlist no longer showed them. Products deleted before the update are taken off the wishlists once on update.
* FIXED: Resolved an issue where the Wishlists block showed four products per row on phones and tablets. On WordPress 7.1 or newer it now shows two per row on tablets and one on phones, the same as the [wpmozo_wishlists] shortcode.
* FIXED: Resolved an issue where the [wpmozo_wishlists] shortcode’s columns_desktop and columns_gutter_desktop attributes were ignored once WPMozo Wishlist (Pro) was active. The columns and columns_gutter spellings Pro uses work too.

2026-10-27 – Version 2.0.1
* IMPROVEMENT: Organized the plugin settings into General, Buttons, Texts, and Styles sub-tabs under WooCommerce > Settings > Wishlist, in line with WooCommerce’s native settings.
* IMPROVEMENT: Settings are now saved using the native WooCommerce Save changes button, matching the rest of the WooCommerce settings screens.
* IMPROVEMENT: Removed the custom header and background from the settings screen to match the native WooCommerce design.
* IMPROVEMENT: The settings now use WooCommerce’s own fields, with checkboxes in place of toggle switches, a number and unit in place of the font size slider, and WordPress’s color picker, and drop the plugin’s custom styling.
* IMPROVEMENT: Rebuilt WooCommerce > Wishlist Insights with native WordPress list tables: search, sortable columns, pagination, and a rows-per-page Screen Option.
* FIXED: Resolved an issue where settings text containing an apostrophe was saved with a backslash.
* FIXED: Resolved an issue where the “Product removed from the wishlist” notification ended with a full stop that the settings screen didn’t show.
* FIXED: An unchanged setting now always uses the default shown on the settings screen, read from one place instead of repeated through the code.

2026-08-31 – Version 2.0.0
* ADDED: Price Drop Badge on the wishlist page to highlight products that have dropped in price since being saved, with customizable text, font size, text color, and an enable/disable option.
* ADDED: Wishlists block for the WordPress block editor with column and gap controls.
* ADDED: Undo option when removing products from the wishlist, replacing the confirmation prompt.
* ADDED: Added controls to choose the move to wishlist button position on the cart page and display it as text, an icon, or both.
* ADDED: Added a configurable “Browse Products” call-to-action for empty wishlists.
* FIXED: Resolved an issue where clearing a color setting using the Clear button was not saved.
* FIXED: Resolved an issue where removing a product from one wishlist instance did not update other wishlist instances on the same page until it was refreshed.
* FIXED: Resolved an issue where a guest’s wishlist cookie was not cleared after the wishlist was emptied.
* FIXED: Resolved an issue where color pickers in the plugin settings lost their transparency slider and Clear button when another theme or plugin registered its own alpha color picker.
* FIXED: Resolved an issue where an open color picker in the plugin settings required two clicks to close.
* IMPROVEMENT: Automatic cleanup of guest wishlists once the visitor’s cookie has expired, so abandoned rows no longer build up in the database.
* IMPROVEMENT: Redesigned wishlist cards by grouping the Add to Cart and Remove actions into a dedicated bottom action row.
* IMPROVEMENT: Moved plugin settings to WooCommerce > Settings > Wishlist instead of a separate top-level menu.
* IMPROVEMENT: Settings are now saved automatically as changes are made.
* IMPROVEMENT: Made the “In Stock” and “Out of Stock” labels on the wishlist page translatable.
* IMPROVEMENT: Rebuilt the plugin core for improved performance and maintainability.

2025-08-05 – Version 1.0.1
* IMPROVEMENT: Compatibility with Astra, Blocksy, Kadence, Hestia, OceanWP, Woostify themes.

2025-07-11 – Version 1.0.0
* Initial release of WPMozo Wishlist Lite for WooCommerce.

upgrade_notice.2.0.1: Settings now use WooCommerce's own fields under WooCommerce > Settings > Wishlist, and Wishlist Insights is rebuilt on WordPress list tables. Your settings are kept. If you use WPMozo Wishlist (Pro), update it to 2.0.1 too.
